claims.text: ALCE is an automatic evaluation benchmark for evaluating LLMs' citation generation.
ALCE's automatic metrics along fluency, correctness, and citation quality correlate strongly with human judgments.
The best evaluated LLM systems lack complete citation support 50% of the time on the ELI5 dataset.

evidence.description: The authors developed automatic metrics along fluency, correctness, and citation quality and demonstrated strong correlation with human judgements.
Experiments show that on the ELI5 dataset, even the best models lack complete citation support 50% of the time.

methodologies.name: ALCE Benchmark
methodologies.description: An end-to-end evaluation benchmark collecting diverse questions and retrieval corpora to measure LLM fluency, correctness, and citation quality automatically.
conditions: end-to-end evidence retrieval and text generation

limitations.text: Existing work relies on commercial search engines and human evaluation, making it challenging to reproduce and compare different modeling approaches.
Even the best evaluated models lack complete citation support 50% of the time on the ELI5 dataset.

future_work.text: Developing better retrievers for citation generation.
Advancing long-context LLMs for citation-backed generation.
Improving the ability of LLMs to synthesize information from multiple sources.
